clue.text: Understood the casket was reserved

parts.note: something understood without being said is tacit
an urn is a casket for ashes

explanation.surface: Someone recalls that a burial casket was quietly set aside for them.
explanation.definitionFit: A taciturn person is quiet and uncommunicative, which is what a reserved person is.

clue.text: Sleeveless coat in the army (Shakespeare)

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
Shakespeare is known as the Bard

explanation.surface: A sleeveless military coat worn in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabard is a short open-sided tunic without sleeves, as worn by heralds or over armour.

clue.text: Mountain dog starts to go on rescue mission

parts.note: a cairn is a small Scottish terrier

indicators.note: the beginnings of the next four words are taken, as 'starts' means opening letters

explanation.surface: A mountain rescue dog sets off on a search mission.
explanation.definitionFit: This peak in Scotland's Cairngorms range gives its name to the range itself.

clue.text: Rent low — put it up for cafe.

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip

indicators.note: in a down clue putting something up means writing it from bottom to top

parts.note: low is the sound a cow makes, a moo

explanation.surface: A café owner, told the rent is low, decides to raise it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid for a property; it is a rip. 'Put it up' turns MOO into OOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearoom is a small restaurant serving tea and light refreshments, much like a café.

clue.text: Have power to control sound

indicators.note: the word sound tells us the wanted word is heard like another

parts.note: a rein is a control, as in keeping a tight rein

explanation.surface: To hold power means to control the noise level.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to rule as a monarch, holding authority over a realm.

clue.text: The rush Victorian ladies used to be in, bringing up the rear!

definitions.text: Victorian ladies used to be in, bringing up the rear!
definitions.meaning: the padded frame worn under the back of a Victorian skirt to puff it out behind

explanation.surface: A rush of Victorian ladies, with the latecomers trailing along behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurry and commotion is one sense; the other is the padded frame that pushed out the back of a nineteenth-century dress.

clue.text: Vessel unties tangled line

indicators.note: tangled means the letters are twisted into a muddle

explanation.surface: A sailor frees a boat's knotted rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but here it means a container for the kitchen; the anagram signal is 'tangled'.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is a household implement, and a vessel is a pot or container for kitchen use.

clue.text: Head-dress helps to make Portia radiant

indicators.note: helps to make says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A jewelled hat makes Portia look glowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental band worn on the head.

clue.text: Issue daily a blank sheet to start work with

definitions.text: a blank sheet to start work with

parts.note: an issue is an outcome or end
a daily is a newspaper

explanation.surface: Hand out a blank sheet every day so staff can begin their tasks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' here is a book: the blank leaf at its front.
explanation.definitionFit: Endpapers are the plain leaves pasted inside a book's cover at its front and back.

clue.text: Spectacle case was upside down in the cutter

parts.note: the frame holds and encases spectacle lenses

indicators.note: in a down clue upside down means written from the bottom up

explanation.surface: A glasses case was found turned over inside a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutter' suggests a boat; it is a tool. 'Upside down' turns WAS into SAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame saw is a cutting tool whose thin blade is held taut in a frame.

clue.text: Etienne, exploited by Conan Doyle

parts.note: Conan Doyle wrote a series of comic stories about a boastful French cavalry officer of Napoleon's army, first name Etienne, and here his title and surname are wanted

explanation.surface: A Frenchman named Etienne was used and taken advantage of by the creator of Sherlock Holmes.
explanation.definitionFit: This hero of Napoleonic adventure tales by the Sherlock Holmes author is a French hussar called Etienne.

clue.text: Reduce below par

definitions.meaning: to cut back gradually, as stocks or a workforce

explanation.surface: Bring your golf score down to less than the standard for the course.
explanation.definitionFit: As a phrasal verb it means cut back or decrease; as an adjective it means worn out and unwell.

clue.text: Scholar gets mark — a black one — from this

definitions.text: Scholar gets mark — a black one — from this

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar's degree
a scar is a mark left on the skin

explanation.surface: A schoolboy is given a black mark as punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: eye make-up leaves a black mark around the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is the dark cosmetic brushed on eyelashes, which leaves a black smudge of colour.

clue.text: Amorphous, having no class

parts.note: a form is a class in a British school
the suffix -less means lacking or without

explanation.surface: A shapeless pupil who has not been put into any class.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amorphous lacks a definite shape or structure.

clue.text: Clot gives doctor nothing to smile wryly about

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the others
wryly means twisted, so these letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A doctor gives a patient no reason to smile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clot' looks like a fool; it is a blockage. 'Wryly' rearranges SMILE to ELISM, and 'about' puts it around MBO.
explanation.definitionFit: An embolism is a blocking of a blood vessel, often by a lodged blood clot.

clue.text: Thread left by the Fair One?

parts.note: Fair Isle is a Shetland island, so the Fair one here is an isle

explanation.surface: A thread abandoned by a beautiful woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Fair One' looks like a beautiful woman; it is Fair Isle, a small island in Shetland famous for patterned knitwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, smooth cotton yarn used for stockings and gloves.

clue.text: How long a spinster can expect to keep well?

definitions.text: How long a spinster can expect to keep well?

parts.words: How long a spinster can expect to keep well?
parts.note: an unmarried woman is said to be left on the shelf, and her time there is read as the period stored goods stay usable

explanation.surface: An unmarried woman wonders how long she will stay healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelf life is the time stored goods remain fit to use, punning on the old phrase for an unmarried woman.

clue.text: Sinister pug

parts.note: sinister is Latin for left, and a pug is a pugilist, so this is a left-handed boxer

explanation.surface: A menacing small dog with a squashed face.
explanation.definitionFit: A southpaw is a left-handed boxer, leading with the right hand.

clue.text: Sailor on his own can provide this sea food

annotationWithheld.why: Sailor on his own can provide this sea food (5) for ORMER: no parse found giving OR+MER or another split from 'Sailor on his own'; searches gave no explanation
annotationWithheld.clue: Sailor on his own can provide this sea food

clue.text: Pity about the Carpenter's mate!

parts.note: re means about or concerning
in Lewis Carroll's poem the Carpenter's companion is the Walrus, and morse is an old word for a walrus

explanation.surface: Sympathy for the Carpenter's companion in Lewis Carroll's poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Pity is an old sense of the answer, as in Shakespeare's 'remorse' meaning compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: In older usage the word meant compassion or tenderness of heart, not only guilt.

clue.text: Become more reckless in fog

definitions.meaning: split as two words, to grow wilder

explanation.surface: A driver grows more careless when visibility is poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means grow wilder; as a single verb it means confuse or perplex, like fogging the mind.

clue.text: Mark time in descent

parts.note: a line is a mark drawn
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Soldiers mark time while going downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage is ancestry, the line of family descent.

clue.text: Niggardly son, heartless fellow, grabs the money

indicators.note: grabs means the first letters close round the word for money
heartless means the middle letter of the word for fellow is dropped

parts.note: a guy is a fellow
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A mean son and a cold-hearted man seize the cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes U from GUY, leaving GY; S and GY then grab TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Niggardly means miserly, mean with money.

clue.text: Article by jolly little man to do with heat

parts.note: the is the definite article
a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
Al is a short form of a man's name such as Alan or Albert

explanation.surface: A grammatical article written by a cheerful short man about warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an adjective; it is old naval slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermal describes anything relating to or caused by heat.

clue.text: Waste one of the Idylls of the King?

definitions.text: one of the Idylls of the King?
definitions.meaning: split and with a dropped aitch it reads as a line from a knight's tale, said of a knight on horseback: he went on horseback

explanation.surface: Is one of Tennyson's Arthurian poems a waste of time?
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's Idylls of the King are full of knights riding out; the question mark flags the punning second sense, 'e rode, a dropped-aitch form of a tale's typical line.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear away or waste gradually; the second sense is a punning past tense of riding.

clue.text: It's an advantage to bridge opponents to split suit

indicators.note: the bridge pair is put into the middle of the word for suit, dividing it

parts.note: to suit is to befit
North and East are opposing players at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Bridge partners gain an edge when their opponents break up a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge North-South play East-West, so N and E sit on opposite sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefit is a gain or helpful factor, which is what an advantage is.

clue.text: Tobacco pipe unsettling the atmosphere in trains

indicators.note: in means the shaken letters sit inside the abbreviation for trains

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former national railway

indicators.note: unsettling suggests these letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: air is the atmosphere

explanation.surface: Pipe smoke fouling the air on railway carriages.
explanation.walkthrough: BR, for British Rail, is a standard crossword shorthand for trains; 'unsettling' is the anagram signal and 'in' places the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A briar is a pipe carved from the root of the tree heath.

clue.text: It takes time to train apricots on trellis work

indicators.note: trellis work is an interlaced criss-cross, telling us to weave these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: training apricot trees up a trellis is slow work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trellis work' rearranges TRAIN, APRICOTS and ON; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting things off wastes days, so delay is something that eats up hours.

clue.text: Bottom of the sound for this fish

indicators.note: the sound of the word means we want what the name is heard as, not how it is spelt

parts.note: Nick Bottom in A Midsummer Night's Dream is a weaver by trade

explanation.surface: A fish that lives at the bottom of a coastal inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom' looks like the seabed and 'sound' like a sea inlet; Bottom is Shakespeare's weaver, and his trade said out loud gives the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The weever is a small sea creature with venomous spines found in sandy shallows.

clue.text: Leaves the putting surface at Rye in a frenzy

parts.note: on a golf course you putt on the green

indicators.note: being in a wild frenzy suggests these letters thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A golfer storms off the green at Rye in a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb; it is foliage. Rye is a town in Sussex with a well-known golf links. 'In a frenzy' rearranges RYE into ERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenery is green foliage and plants, a mass of leaves.
